posts.name: Koga
posts.cooked:
One problem with Ambuscade is if he's on his flip side and he plays his cloaking device, (mostly due to an out of turn effect) he flips back to front side and if you just leave it out there he never flips back. His trap plays always seem like dead turns too.

So I decided to make an oversized card using my templates with a few additional rules. One to fix him and the other to make him a bit stronger. The second addition I took from The Matriarch's new printing on how she handles fowl cards. So if Ambuscade gets lucky he could end up playing multiple traps in one turn.

Front side:

At the start of the villain turn, if the personal cloaking device is in play, flip Ambuscade's villain character card.

Both sides:

Whenever a trap card is played from the villain deck, play the top card of the villain deck.

posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked: I had a decent game with ambuscade a while back, and it got me thinking. Thematically, he should just start off more set-up. His set-up play in the game included his cloaking device and his rocket launcher, starting out with him invisible felt really good to me since it spoke strongly to him having ambushed us. I think maybe a variant (including Koga's suggestion for reworking the cloaking device) of making his cloaking device guarenteed in set-up and pre-arming one or both of his traps would do a lot to make him feel like he was just lying in wait for you to enter his web. Don't know how it would actually work out though since I haven't tried it and I haven't played him much overall.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Koga:

One problem with Ambuscade is if he's on his flip side and he plays his cloaking device, (mostly due to an out of turn effect) he flips back to front side and if you just leave it out there he never flips back.

That's certainly a weird glitch, but it should virtually never happen.  He can't stay on his flipside unless the PCD is in play at the start of his turn, so the only way this could ever happen would be if you somehow caused the PCD to leave play and come back into play before the next turn.  Into the Stratosphere + Timeshift, perhaps.  It's enough of a niche case that I wouldn't worry about it.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked: Ambuscade really benefits from DR, hence why his Advanced mode is really a nicely balanced fight. The reason why his traps feel like dead cards usually is because he simply goes down too fast and the traps dont have a chance to be played. His the extra DR + shield is a nasty combo that will take a few turns to fix. He has a little bit of deck acceleration, but just slightly under what I think would make traps a more consistent threat.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Virtually every time I play him, I intend to apply his Advanced text and then forget.  Somehow this never happens with Voss or Akashbhuta.  I think seeing that pitifully tiny 50 HP makes me want to go for the throat.

The most fun I ever have with Ambuscade is when he chains multiple Run and Guns, Quick Stim-Patches, Snatch & Grabs, and the like.  I think this playstyle is far more fun and unique, and the Traps and Devices are a distraction from it, making him play more like too many other villains.  If he gets a lot of these cards instead, he feels more like a hunter, who knows he's a bit squishy but is too smart to make himself a target, so he keeps dancing around, staying on his toes and keeping the heroes on theirs...a very feisty, high-energy fight.  A pity it doesn't usually work out that way.  Most of his Devices are a joke, and the Traps just aren't worth how long you have to wait for them.

posts.cooked: Turn 1, Hand-Cannon always lets the heroes pick (granted, they'll most likely pick highest-HP anyway), while Turret only gives as many choices as there are tied heroes.  (Note to self: play original Fixer, DW Nightmist, Chrono-Ranger, original Bunker, and Team Leader Tachyon some game.)  After that, of course, it's more of a crapshoot...but most heroes can't get more than 1 card into play per turn, so the rate of change tends to be small, with each hero who plays a one-shot falling behind the ones who play an O/E.  Of course, sometimes the O/E is a Driving Mantis.  :)

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Two recent ideas we tried had him play the top card of his deck whenever an environment card was destroyed, and had his traps destroy hero cards, Unavoidable Explosive destroying (H) cards, and Rigged to Detonate destroying all the cards of the hero it hits.  

That fast furious game play went a lot faster that game.  I found it fitting with Ambuscade being the anit-Haka, that he'd also gain from environment being destroyed.  The traps destroying cards made them actually scary, combining both he was no slouch, burning his deck, and making you nervous that those traps were going to destroy all your stuff.

We also used the shuffle a trap play a card rule, but we do that so much we don't even think of it as a house rule anymore.

posts.name: jmrburgard
posts.cooked:
The variant I've tried is a more substantial modification (on par w/ Mad Bomber Blade):

The basic idea is that Ambuscade, as a hunter, prepares before he engages and then focuses on one target. The rest of it is just to distract the people he is not hunting. 

Setup: Find H-1 traps and insert them face up.

Front Side: Every time a hero plays a card reveal the top card of the villain deck. If it is a trap or a device, play it. Other wise shuffle it into the deck. At the end of the villain turn, if there are H devices in play, flip Ambuscade.

(Advanced: At the end of the villain turn, reveal the top card of the villain deck. If it is a trap or a device, play it.)

Back Side: Ambuscade is immune to damage from every hero except for the hero with the highest hit points at the start of the villain turn. Redirect all damage dealt by Ambuscade to the hero with the highest hit points at the start of the villain turn. When a villian card would be played Ambuscade regains H hit points and deals the hero with the highest hit points H projectile damage. And the end of the villain turn deal the hero with the highest hit points 5-X energy damage, where X is the number of devices in play. At the end of the villain turn if the personal cloaking device is not in play and there are fewer than H devices in play, flip Ambuscade. 

(Advanced: At the start of the villain turn Ambuscade deals the Hero target with the highest hit points H-2 fire damage).
